article_title: Assessment Design in the GenAI Era: The X1-X2-X3 Assessment Pattern for Testing Students' AI Literacy, Learning Outcomes, and Reflection
citation: Riasat Islam and Thomas Roelleke (2026). Assessment Design in the GenAI Era: The X1-X2-X3 Assessment Pattern for Testing Students' AI Literacy, Learning Outcomes, and Reflection. https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.12351
title: The X1-X2-X3 three-part response structure for AI-integrated assessment
description: A three-part response structure for assessments that permit web and GenAI use. X1 requires a sourced extract with evidence: "a concise extract from the sourced answer, source identification, timestamp, and a mandatory full-screen screenshot". X2 requires the student's own answer plus an account of how it differs from the sourced answer. X3 requires a brief reflection on what was learned and a bounded quality rating of the sourced answer with justification. The pattern was stabilized across four deployments and scored with an 18-point rubric mapped across the three fields.
requirements: Mandatory full-screen readable screenshot showing the sourced answer, current question, and student response fields
Word limits (100 words for X1a, 200 for X2, 100 for X3 in the practice exam) and a reusable rubric applied consistently across markers
constraints: The design required substantial teaching-team effort shifted into assessment design, evidence checking, and more interpretive marking
The exam format was very new to students, and early iterations showed incomplete triads and weak reflection
target_learners: second-year undergraduate database systems students in a large cohort (270 students)
target_learning_goals: AI literacy and evaluative judgement about sourced answers
examples: In the final exam the format was embedded in a mixed traditional/Web-GenAI online exam with an 18-point rubric converted to 6 or 9 marks per question depending on weighting
